title: Compensated Current Choice and Counterfactual Identification
description: Archival release and current endpoint of the Rational Relapse Theory research program. The paper studies what a target environment's baseline current choice and available compensated comparison support can identify when nearby target comparisons required for a direct local comparative static are missing. Standard compensated-choice measurement, cancellation, graph and cycle-space arguments, rank/kernel methods, finite differences, implicit-function comparative statics, and standard dynamic consequences are treated as background infrastructure. The substantive focus is the information structure and comparison support required to identify counterfactual local choice responses. The release includes the English manuscript and a Chinese archival translation of the same v9.0 scholarly object.
